status: draft v0.1 — original items, not validated, not piloted
note: Format test for PLAN-notes-02-reactivity.md. All items written from scratch; none derived from Braverman's copyrighted questionnaire.

responseScales.notApplicable: Reactivity items offer 'Doesn't apply / I avoid this' which is recorded, not scored.

traitScales.name: Drive
traitScales.definition: Exploration plus willingness to expend effort for reward. Merges the 'Seeker' and 'Engine' dimensions.
traitScales.basis: DeYoung 2013 (Plasticity); Treadway 2012 (effort for reward); BAS Drive/Fun Seeking
traitScales.timeframe: In general, over the past few years

items.text: I start things nobody asked me to start.
When something interests me, I'll put in work that others would find tedious.
I'd rather stick with what already works than try an unfamiliar option.
I go looking for new information even when nothing requires it.
I lose interest once the novelty of a project wears off.
I'll take on a harder task if the payoff is bigger.
I often decide something isn't worth the effort.
I have more things I want to do than time to do them.
I'm content to let other people set the direction.
I keep working on a problem after other people have set it aside.

reactivityAxes.name: Sleep reactivity
reactivityAxes.question: How much does short or broken sleep change you?
reactivityAxes.evidenceAnchor: Sleep loss degrades motivation and emotion regulation; insomnia tracks depression risk (ISI literature)
reactivityAxes.timeframe: Think about the day after a night of clearly less sleep than usual

items.text: After a short night, my mood the next day is...
After a short night, my patience with other people is...
After a short night, my ability to start tasks is...
I can have two or three bad nights in a row and still feel like myself.

reactivityAxes.name: Stimulant reactivity
reactivityAxes.question: How much do caffeine and nicotine move you?
reactivityAxes.evidenceAnchor: Adenosine/dopamine; large individual differences in caffeine sensitivity

items.text: After caffeine, my focus is...
After caffeine later in the day, my sleep that night is...
On a day with no caffeine at all, I feel...
I can drink coffee at night and sleep fine.

reactivityAxes.name: Alcohol reactivity
reactivityAxes.question: How much does alcohol, and the day after, move you?
reactivityAxes.evidenceAnchor: GABA-A action; next-day rebound anxiety; GLP-1 craving trials show reward-pathway involvement

items.text: The day after drinking, my anxiety is...
The day after drinking, my mood is...
While drinking, how much I say or do things I wouldn't otherwise is...
A couple of drinks makes no real difference to how I feel the next day.

reactivityAxes.name: Cycle and hormonal reactivity
reactivityAxes.question: How much do hormonal shifts move you?
reactivityAxes.evidenceAnchor: PMDD add-back studies (Schmidt 1998; AJP 2017): symptoms triggered by change in ovarian steroids, not by level; hormonal contraception and depression risk (Skovlund)
reactivityAxes.gating: Shown only if the context intake indicates it applies; must be skippable without penalty

items.text: In the week before my period, my mood is...
In the week before my period, my irritability is...
When I've started or stopped hormonal birth control, my mood was...
My mood is about the same at every point in my cycle.

reactivityAxes.name: Stress reactivity
reactivityAxes.question: How much does acute stress or conflict move you, and how long does it last?
reactivityAxes.evidenceAnchor: Cortisol effects on memory encoding and metacognition; noradrenaline and risk-taking

items.text: After a tense conversation, how long it takes me to settle is...
Under time pressure, the quality of my decisions is...
During a stressful week, my sleep is...
Stressful events roll off me within an hour or two.

reactivityAxes.name: Reward-cue reactivity
reactivityAxes.question: How much do cues — food, shopping, games, notifications — pull at you?
reactivityAxes.evidenceAnchor: Ghrelin/leptin and food-cue reactivity; dopamine-agonist impulse control disorders; GLP-1 craving reduction

items.text: I buy or order something within minutes of first seeing it.
When I'm hungry, food I hadn't been thinking about becomes hard to ignore.
I keep playing, scrolling or watching well past the point I meant to stop.
I can have something tempting in the house and not think about it.

reactivityAxes.name: Social reactivity
reactivityAxes.question: How much do connection and rejection move you?
reactivityAxes.evidenceAnchor: μ-opioid receptor availability and attachment style (Nummenmaa/Tuominen)

items.text: After being left out or turned down, my mood for the rest of the day is...
After a few days with little contact with people I'm close to, I feel...
After a warm conversation with someone I care about, my mood is...
I can go a week without seeing anyone close to me and feel no different.

openIssues: shift5 asks for magnitude but items 'my mood is...' imply direction — either split into magnitude+direction, or reword each item so the anchor is unambiguous ('how different is your mood').
Every reactivity axis currently has 3 positive + 1 reverse item; aim for 2/2 to balance acquiescence.
react_stim_03 ('on a day with no caffeine') measures withdrawal, not sensitivity. Possibly a separate sub-construct.
Cycle axis needs careful wording for people on continuous contraception, post-menopause, trans and nonbinary users; gating must not feel like an assumption about the user.
Reward-cue axis overlaps with the Restraint trait scale — check discriminant validity in the pilot; if they correlate above ~.7 they're one thing.
Should reactivity items ask 'how much does X move you' (perceived sensitivity) or 'how often does X happen' (frequency)? Current draft mixes both scales across axes, which may not be comparable.
Need a floor: people who never drink, never use caffeine, etc. should not get a low score — record as not applicable and exclude from the profile.
